result:
Wave 1 (piece 01, skeleton and storage) is finished, and all 9 tests pass. `.brigade/context.md` still matches the code, so it needed no changes. I wrote the prompts for wave 2 in `.brigade/prompts/02-importers.md`, `03-rules.md` and `04-budgets.md`, and added these pieces to the table in `.brigade/plan.md`.

| Wave | Piece | Model | Effort | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | 02 importers | sonnet | medium | Handles money parsing and imports a file all-or-nothing. The prompt decides the edge cases, the tests catch errors, and the final opus review covers it. |
| 2 | 03 rules | sonnet | medium | The precedence rules are clear and the prompt fixes the details. Easy to test. |
| 2 | 04 budgets | sonnet | medium | Simple totals, easy to test. |
| 3 | 05 cli + final review | sonnet, then opus | medium | Outline only for now. It gets written by `/brigade next` once wave 2 is done. |

The spec left some details open, so each prompt settles them, and each session should follow those choices rather than decide again. For example, an amount with more than two decimal places is rejected rather than rounded. A zenith amount with a minus sign counts as malformed. Two identical rows in one file are both imported.

The three pieces don't share any code files. The only shared files are `context.md` and `progress.md`, which each session only adds to. You can run the pieces one after another, or run them at the same time in separate worktrees and merge those two files by hand.

Start with:

    claude --model sonnet --effort medium "Do brigade piece 02: follow .brigade/prompts/02-importers.md"

Then run pieces 03 and 04 with the same command, changing the piece number and file to `03-rules.md` and `04-budgets.md`. When all three are done, run `/brigade next` to get the wave 3 prompts.
